clue.text: Spare place that's used by cook at sea?

definitions.text: Spare place that's used by cook at sea?

parts.words: Spare place that's used by cook at sea?
parts.note: a spare is knocking down all ten pins with two balls, so the spare place is where tenpins is played; the cook at sea hints that a ship's kitchen sits at the end of the phrase

explanation.surface: A puzzle about some spare room on board ship that the cook uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' reads as 'extra', but here it is the tenpin term; a ship's kitchen is a galley, which ends the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare is a tenpin score, and the venue where tenpin is played has lanes, pins and a bar.

clue.text: Billionaire's first to not offer tip in bar

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word Billionaire's is taken

parts.note: to lack something is to be without it and so have none to offer
to tip, like a ship, is to lean over to one side, to list

explanation.surface: A billionaire refusing to leave a tip in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to exclude them, exactly what putting a name on a banned register does.

clue.text: Seaside town us kids mark for investment

parts.note: us, first person plural, as the subject pronoun we

indicators.note: investment is the act of clothing or enclosing, so one piece is wrapped in the other

parts.note: kids are young people collectively, youth
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A resort town where we children are given money to invest.
explanation.walkthrough: WEYMOUTH is a seaside resort in Dorset, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dorset resort sits on the English Channel coast with a long sandy beach.

clue.text: Fill one's sad line out

parts.note: one's, as said by the speaker, is I'm (I am)

indicators.note: out tells us that one letter is to be thrown away from the word for sad

parts.note: blue means sad or downhearted

explanation.surface: Someone sorrowfully telling a pal to fill in a line that's been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M BLUE ('one's sad') loses its L, leaving IMBUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to permeate or saturate, as with colour or feeling.

clue.text: Supply Middle East storage — one of these?

definitions.text: Supply Middle East storage — one of these?

indicators.note: supply read as the adverb of supple, bendily, so the letters are flexed into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Middle Eastern supply depot is one of these tanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as a verb but is the adverb 'supply' (in a supple way), signalling an anagram of ME plus STORAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas holder is a large storage tank for fuel, often seen on old industrial skylines.

clue.text: One used to scream at rat, initially, with cat circling

indicators.note: circling means the cat word goes around the two letters

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the words at and rat

explanation.surface: Someone screaming at a rat while a cat prowls round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box is the organ that produces a scream or any other vocal sound.

clue.text: It sounds like your setter got a duck

indicators.note: the clue openly says that what follows is a matter of how it is pronounced

parts.note: your setter is the crossword compiler, I; got a is had a, so I had a contracts to I'd a

explanation.surface: The setter confessing to having acquired a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'd a' said quickly gives the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck, famed for the soft down used in quilts.

clue.text: I can't stop cat — did monkeys?

indicators.note: to monkey with something is to mess about with it, so the letters are fiddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone helpless to stop a cat, wondering whether monkeys did it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked who is unable to give up a habit would say they can't stop.

clue.text: Currently, warship tails every other one

indicators.note: every other one takes alternate letters of the words warship tails, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A warship currently being followed by every other vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the present state of affairs, as things now stand.

clue.text: Record why Sally's left

indicators.note: left means the word is read leftwards, from right to left, in this across answer

parts.note: a sally is a sudden sortie by troops, a raid
Y sounds like why, the usual crossword letter for it

explanation.surface: A record of why someone called Sally walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but is the noun for a military sortie.
explanation.definitionFit: A journal is a daily record of events kept by its writer.

clue.text: Is on horse jockey targets at meeting?

definitions.meaning: to sit astride a mount with a leg on each side
at a race meeting a rider aims for the finest mounts on the card, read as two words

explanation.surface: A rider in the saddle aiming for wins at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as BEST RIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle something, as a rider sits astride a mount, is the verb's plain sense.

clue.text: Trying one end of cigar — smoke's blown

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: end of takes only the final letter of the word cigar
blown means scattered about, so the letters are blown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Cigar smoke drifting about is an irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying here means annoying or wearing on the patience, as a tiresome task is.

clue.text: Perfect flipping time to spread feature on mosque

indicators.note: the perfect word is spread apart to hold the other piece

parts.note: mint means in perfect, as-new condition

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone cursing that this is the perfect time to spread something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' poses as a mild British expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: The slender tower from which the call to prayer is given stands beside or on a mosque.

clue.text: Social media users write tat — it's awful

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: it's supplies the word it, the 's being is, a link

explanation.surface: A sneer that people online churn out awful rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a jokey term for prominent, prolific users of one microblogging site, modelled on literati.

clue.text: Bits of house reportedly suffering from inflexibility

indicators.note: reportedly means the answer is said like the words for parts of a house

parts.note: two parts of a house: a room and an attic

explanation.surface: Bits of a house said to be suffering from stiffness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatism makes joints stiff and painful, so a sufferer is stiff and inflexible.

clue.text: Like holding flash book

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
a mo is a moment, a flash

explanation.surface: Someone liking to hold a flashy book.
explanation.walkthrough: AMOS is a book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the minor prophets' books in the Old Testament of the Bible.

clue.text: Manufactured feeling was clearly explained

parts.note: manufactured means made
a sense is a feeling, as a sense of unease

explanation.surface: A manufactured emotion that was clearly put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that was intelligible and came across clearly was understandable.

clue.text: One's blooming great desire in the morning, after getting up

indicators.note: getting up in a down answer means the pieces are read from bottom to top, done after they are assembled

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, great, with the 1 written as I
to long is to desire
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone's great urge to bloom on rising in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's blooming' reads as an exclamation but defines a flowering tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree or shrub bears large showy flowers in spring, so it is something in bloom.

clue.text: Figures sold at auction houses

indicators.note: houses means the words contain the answer in their letters

explanation.surface: Sales figures for houses sold at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and statistics, numbers collected for analysis, are figures.

clue.text: Stew in France, said to touch that woman

indicators.note: to touch means to be next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: dit is French for said
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A French stew said to be touching some woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' is the noun for a state of agitation, not a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is to be in a state of nervous agitation, unable to decide.

clue.text: British nurses agree about study in local area

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the British letters cradle the other piece
about means around in a rearranged way, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: British nurses agreeing about where to study in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for one's nearby pub, so its outdoor area is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the local is one's neighbourhood pub, and its outdoor drinking space is that pub's area.

clue.text: Most recent points

definitions.meaning: a string of compass points: north, east, west, east, south, top

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense spells N, E, W, E, S, T as six compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of new describes the latest arrival or most recent version.

clue.text: Believe paper reported those rowing in this

indicators.note: reported means the answer is said like the words for believe and paper

parts.note: to buy a story is to believe it; a ream is a quantity of paper

explanation.surface: Believing what a newspaper reported about rowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' suggests a newspaper, but it is a ream of sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme is an ancient galley with two banks of oars, so oarsmen row in it.

clue.text: Travelling to old city is start of mission

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter of the word mission

explanation.surface: A trip to an ancient city as the beginning of a mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourism is travelling for pleasure, the industry of visitors and sightseeing.

clue.text: Growth areas of computer industry

indicators.note: of here means taken out of the words, the answer lying inside them

explanation.surface: The expanding sectors of the computer business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth areas' sounds like business jargon but means wombs, where foetuses grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombs are the organs in which a foetus grows, so they are areas of growth.

clue.text: Cutter's crew was almost retired

parts.note: hands are crew members on a ship

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters run backwards
almost means the word was loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A cutter's crew was nearly all pensioned off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' looks like a boat, but is a tool; the 's is 'is', so the definition reads 'Cutter is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw used with one hand is a tool for cutting wood.

clue.text: Being in slavery topped everything

indicators.note: topped means beheaded, the first letter removed from the top of this down word

parts.note: the lot means everything

explanation.surface: Slavery as the thing that beat everything.
explanation.walkthrough: A helot was a serf of ancient Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: Helots were the state-owned serfs of ancient Sparta, so one is a person in bondage.

clue.text: Simple iron, say … ball's out of bounds

parts.note: iron is an example of a chemical element

indicators.note: out of bounds drops the outer letters of the word ball, its bounds

explanation.surface: A golfer's iron shot sends the ball out of bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' and 'out of bounds' suggest golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means basic or fundamental, not compound, so simple.

clue.text: Description of Els's scores

parts.note: the golfer Ernie Els's surname can be built by putting L into ES, which the four plus one letter answer spells as a phrase

explanation.surface: A description of golfer Ernie Els's scores.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as the instruction 'L in ES': it builds ELS. Ernie Els is a South African golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scores are marks scratched or drawn on a surface, which are strokes or lines.

clue.text: Cheese somewhat overlapping edge of base for celebrity chef

indicators.note: the two words partly overlap, so the end of the cheese is shifted to sit within the edge word

parts.note: ricotta is a soft Italian cheese
a verge is an edge, as a grass verge

explanation.surface: Cheese spilling over the edge of a base for a TV chef.
explanation.walkthrough: RICOTTA and VERGE interleave: RI, VER, COTTA, GE. River Cottage is the Dorset farm and TV series of chef Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall.
explanation.definitionFit: River Cottage is the farm and restaurant headquarters of the TV cook Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall.
